questions.question: Double trailers compared to single trailers:

options.text: Are less likely to roll over.
Need more time to react to hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need more time to react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Double and triple trailers jackknife and roll over more easily than single trailers. Drivers must look far ahead and react to hazards early. Slow down gradually and change lanes slowly.

questions.question: Using a helper when backing up a large vehicle is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Encouraged.
questions.explanation: Backing a large vehicle is always dangerous because you cannot see well behind you. Using a helper to watch your blind spots is encouraged whenever possible.

questions.question: If spring brakes activate while hauling a heavy load, a complete stop will:

options.text: Take a short amount of time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a long time.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes do not work on all axles. When they activate because air pressure is low, your vehicle will need extra distance to stop, especially with a heavy load.

questions.question: If you are not sure your vehicle fits under a bridge or sign, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Drive more slowly.
questions.explanation: If you are unsure whether your vehicle will fit under overhead objects, slow down and find a different route if possible.

questions.question: What can happen if the exhaust system does not work properly?

options.text: Poisonous fumes may enter the cab.
Fumes may exit the rear of the muffler.

questions.correctAnswerText: Poisonous fumes may enter the cab.
questions.explanation: Leaks in the exhaust system are very dangerous. They allow toxic fumes into the cab or sleeper berth, which can harm drivers and passengers.

questions.question: During a trip, landing gear should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Completely raised.
questions.explanation: Landing gear must always be completely raised before driving. If not fully raised, it can catch on railroad tracks or other road hazards.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS):

options.text: Are only used on trucks carrying hazardous materials.
Help drivers maintain control while braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help drivers maintain control while braking.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheels from locking up when you brake hard. This helps you stay in control.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with power steering, make sure that:

options.text: The fluid is at the proper level.
The hoses are connected to the battery.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fluid is at the proper level.
questions.explanation: When inspecting a power steering system, check the hoses, pump, and fluid level. Look for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: If a vehicle begins to hydroplane, the driver should:

options.text: Release the accelerator and push in the clutch.
Push in the clutch and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator and push in the clutch.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, release the accelerator and push in the clutch to regain control.

questions.question: When going downhill, brake until your vehicle reaches a speed that is:
questions.correctAnswerText: 5 mph below your safe speed.
questions.explanation: On a downhill grade, hold the brake pedal until your vehicle slows to 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the brakes. Repeat this process as needed.

questions.question: Fully-loaded trucks:

options.text: Are less likely to roll over than empty trucks.
Are more likely to roll over than empty trucks.
Are just as likely to roll over as empty trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are more likely to roll over than empty trucks.
questions.explanation: Fully-loaded trucks roll over more easily than empty trucks. The heavy cargo raises the center of gravity.

questions.question: When traveling slower than 40 mph, keep at least ____ of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle length.
questions.correctAnswerText: One second
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, allow one second of space for every 10 feet of vehicle length. At faster speeds, use the same formula and add one more second. Large vehicles need more space to stop than small ones.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should check your mirrors:
questions.correctAnswerText: More often than usual.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. Before changing lanes, check them even more carefully.

questions.question: If the emergency air line loses pressure:

options.text: The Anti-Lock Braking System will turn on.
The service air line will turn on.
The emergency brakes will turn on.

questions.correctAnswerText: The emergency brakes will turn on.
questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes. If air pressure is lost in the emergency line, the emergency trailer brakes activate automatically.

questions.question: In a double or triple combination, the ____ trailer should be closest to the cab.
questions.correctAnswerText: Heaviest
questions.explanation: Put the heaviest trailer closest to the tractor. Put the lightest trailer at the back.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve releases air from the air brake system:

options.text: The air pressure is too high.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air pressure is too high.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air when pressure gets too high. If this happens, something is wrong and needs to be fixed by a mechanic.

questions.question: If you see taillights while driving in fog:

options.text: The lights may not show where the road is. The vehicle may have left the road.
You can be sure the vehicle is on the road.
The lights may be an optical illusion.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lights may not show where the road is. The vehicle may have left the road.
questions.explanation: In fog, don't trust lights to show where the road is. A vehicle's lights may come from a vehicle that left the roadway.

questions.question: When driving in heavy traffic, the safest speed is:

options.text: The speed of the traffic around you.
Much slower than the surrounding traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The speed of the traffic around you.
questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, match the speed of other vehicles. Vehicles moving at the same speed are less likely to crash. Do not exceed the speed limit.

questions.question: Regular vehicle inspections keep you safe by checking:
questions.correctAnswerText: Safety.
questions.explanation: The main reason to inspect your vehicle is safety. It protects you and other drivers on the road.

questions.question: Brake fade happens when:
questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes are used too much.
questions.explanation: Overusing brakes makes them too hot. This heat causes them to fade and work less well.
